item.title: 🇷🇺 Today, September 8, we mark the Day of the Languages of the Peoples of Russia for the first time.
item.description: 🇷🇺 Today, September 8, we mark the Day of the Languages of the Peoples of Russia for the first time. The main goal of the holiday is to preserve and support Russia’s linguistic diversity , promote native languages, and strengthen interethnic harmony and respect for the cultures of all the peoples of our country. Russia fosters more than 150 languages , each of which is an invaluable cultural heritage of the peoples of our nation. *** 🔹 More than 190 peoples live in Russia, each with its own cultural and linguistic traditions. There are more than 270 different languages and dialects in total, which can be divided into several major groups: • Slavic languages. Russian is the state language and the most widely spoken language. • Turkic languages. These include Tatar, Bashkir and Chuvash. • Finno-Ugric languages. These include Mari, Udmurt and Komi. • Caucasian languages. These include Avar, Chechen and Ingush. • Paleoasiatic languages. These include Chukchi and Koryak. 🔹 105 languages are represented in the education system: 24 are used as languages of instruction, while 81 are taught as academic subjects. 🔹 Russian is the state language and the most widely spoken language throughout the country. 🔹 The rarest languages of the peoples of Russia include Itelmen and Copper Island Aleut , each of which has only one competent speaker remaining. Several other languages have fewer than ten speakers , including the Orok language on Sakhalin, Negidal and Udege languages in Khabarovsk Kra

several major groups:
• Slavic languages.

• Turkic languages.
These include Tatar, Bashkir and Chuvash.
• Finno-Ugric languages.
These include Mari, Udmurt and Komi.
• Caucasian languages.
These include Avar, Chechen and Ingush.
• Paleoasiatic languages.
These include Chukchi and Koryak.

🇺🇳
September 8
marks
the 25th anniversary of the adoption in 2001 of
the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action
, which have become fundamental international legal instruments for combating racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance.
The Russian Federation, which was directly involved in developing these instruments,
consistently reaffirms its commitment to the spirit and letter of these agreements
, aimed at ensuring equality for all and protecting human dignity.
Russia’s consistent support for translating the outcomes of the Durban Conference into action is reflected, among other things, in its
co-sponsorship of the UN General Assembly resolution
“A global call for concrete action for the elimination of racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance and the comprehensive implementation of and follow-up to the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action”
, introduced annually by the Group of 77 and China.
☝️
A quarter of a century later, the
Durban Declaration and Programme of Action
are
more relevant and significant than ever
.
The Russian Federation actively draws on these documents in its
flagship UN General Assembly initiative
,
“Combating glorification of Nazism, neo-Nazism and other practices that contribute to fuelling contemporary forms of racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance”
.
In particular, the first paragraph of
the Russian resolution
states
:
“Reaffirms the relevant provisions of the Durban Declaration and of the outcome document of the Durban Review Conference, in which States condemned the persistence and resurgence of neo-Nazism, neo-Fascism and violent nationalist ideologies based on racial and national prejudice and stated that those phenomena could never be justified in any instance or in any circumstances”.
❗️
We are compelled to note that certain states are now attempting to revise the fundamental principles enshrined in
the Declaration
.
In this regard, we would like to recall that the destructive practice of imposing the concept of “civilizational exceptionalism”, manifestations of neocolonial revanchism, and any divisions along national, cultural, religious or other lines
serve only to destabilise the framework of international law built over decades
, which has become one of the pillars of global stability and security.
The substance of the Durban process is reflected in Russia’s cooperation agenda with African states. Overcoming the legacy of colonialism, ensuring sovereign equality and developing common approaches to building a fairer,
#MultipolarWorld
are
among the priorities of
the Third Russia-Africa Summit
, scheduled to take place in Moscow on October 28-29.

⚡️
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's comment on the International Day of Journalists’ Solidarity
(September 8, 2026)
💬
September 8 marks the International Day of Journalists’ Solidarity.
The date was established in 1958 in memory of
Czechoslovak anti-fascist journalist Julius Fucik
, who was executed by the Nazis in 1943. It serves as a reminder of the importance of freedom of speech and professional journalism, while also drawing attention to the safety of media workers and the need for solidarity and mutual support within the global journalistic community.
In recent years, these fundamental principles have been increasingly eroded by the West’s policy of
purging the media landscape of unwelcome viewpoints in pursuit of narrow political goals
.
👉
Russian media outlets abroad have faced
systematic harassment and various forms of repression
in countries whose leaders routinely proclaim their commitment to press freedom while grandly portraying themselves as a “flourishing garden”.
In practice, under far-fetched pretexts, they have
blocked
Russian television channels,
shut down
correspondent offices and
expelled
journalists.
The Kiev regime has launched an outright campaign against Russian journalists reporting truthful, first-hand information.
At the same time,
the neo-Nazi junta’s openly declared intent to kill civilians
– a category that under international law includes media workers – has drawn not the slightest criticism from its Western patrons.
Terrorist attacks have claimed the lives of
:
▪️
Igor Kornelyuk
▪️
Anton Voloshin
▪️
Andrey Stenin
▪️
Anatoly Klyan
▪️
Daria Dugina
▪️
Oleg Klokov
▪️
Maxim Fomin
(Vladlen Tatarsky)
▪️
Rostislav Zhuravlev
▪️
Boris Maksudov
▪️
Semyon Yeryomin
▪️
Valery Kozhin
▪️
Nikita Tsisagi
▪️
Yulia Kuznetsova
▪️
Alexander Martemyanov
▪️
Alexander Fedorchak
▪️
Andrey Panov
▪️
Anna Prokofyeva
▪️
Nikita Goldin
▪️
Ivan Zuev
Dozens of media workers
have also been wounded
while carrying out their professional duties.
It is deeply troubling that these crimes and acts of repression have failed to elicit an adequate response from the Western media community
. Mainstream outlets in those countries, guided by political expediency and in defiance of the principles of journalistic solidarity,
chose to remain silent
and act as though the issue did not concern them. In doing so, they abandoned professional ethics and the very idea of solidarity among journalists.
Those who nevertheless found the courage to defend Russian media workers or honour the memory of those who died for the truth were met with
a barrage of criticism and accusations
, including from fellow journalists.
***
❗️
We call on the global media community to show solidarity with their Russian colleagues and speak out in their defence against politically motivated repression by Western countries.
For our part, we will continue
to consistently defend the rights
of Russian journalists abroad and
seek justice for crimes
committed against Russian correspondents.

📆
From September 7 to October 7, Geneva will host
the 63rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council
.
The Session
is expected to address
a broad range of issues
on the international human rights agenda, including:
• protection and promotion of economic, social and cultural rights,
• ensuring the right to development,
• protection of children,
• combating discrimination against women,
• advancing the interests of indigenous peoples,
• preventing the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures on the enjoyment of human rights, as well as other thematic issues.
At Russia’s initiative, a high-level thematic discussion will be held to mark the
60th anniversary of the adoption of the International Covenants on Human Rights
.
The Council will adopt
the outcomes of the Universal Periodic Review of the national reports
of Belgium, Denmark, Latvia, Namibia, Niger, Nicaragua, Mozambique, Palau, Paraguay, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Singapore, Somalia, Sierra Leone and Estonia.
At the initiative of the EU, the Council will once again consider
a
politicised and highly confrontational
draft resolution
on the human rights situation in Russia, aimed at extending for another year the mandate of the relevant HRC Special Rapporteur,
Mariana Katzarova
of Bulgaria.
❗️
Russia’s stance on this matter
remains unchanged
: we do not recognise the mandate of this illegitimate special procedure, and any form of interaction with it is unacceptable to us.
The Russian delegation, which will participate in the Session
as an observer
, intends, as before, to make active use of all available opportunities
to overcome confrontation
and
promote a unifying agenda
, as well as
to foster among international partners an understanding of the importance of establishing constructive international dialogue
on the promotion and protection of human rights, with due respect for the national, religious, cultural and historical characteristics of every state.
A number of special side events
will be organised to present Russia’s approaches to the most pressing issues on the session’s agenda to the international community.

The fighting began early in the morning and raged throughout the day. Napoleon repeatedly committed fresh forces in an attempt to break the Russian army, but the French failed to crush Russian resistance . Despite losses, Russian regiments continued to fight with extraordinary determination, contesting every key position. By the end of the day, Napoleon had failed to achieve his principal objective – the destruction of the Russian army. 📆
September 8 marks a Day of Military Glory of Russia – the anniversary of the Battle of
#Borodino
.
On September 7, 1812, near the village of Borodino, some 120 kilometres west of Moscow, the Russian army under
Mikhail Kutuzov
faced Napoleon’s invading Grande Armée.
⚔️
The Battle of Borodino became the largest and bloodiest single-day battle of
the Patriotic War of 1812
, with well over 200,000 troops engaged on both sides.
The fighting began early in the morning and raged throughout the day. Napoleon repeatedly committed fresh forces in an attempt to break the Russian army, but
the French failed to crush Russian resistance
.
Despite losses, Russian regiments continued to fight with extraordinary determination, contesting every key position. By the end of the day,
Napoleon had failed to achieve his principal objective – the destruction of the Russian army.
The losses of the European invaders were even heavier, and although, the battlefield was for the moment theirs,
Russian forces retreated in full order, having preserved the army and manpower
.
Borodino became an enduring symbol of courage, resilience and devotion to the Fatherland
, while the soldiers and commanders who fought there entered Russian history forever.
✍️
As the great Russian writer
Mikhail Lermontov
wrote in his 1837 poem
Borodino
:
“That all of Russia remembers – no less,
About the day of Borodino…
You are not to see such struggles!..
Banners whirled round, like shadows,
Against the smoke the shots would blaze,
Sounds of steel, screams of gunfire,
Warriors’ hands starting to tire,
And cannonball’s flight would mire,
The bloody mound that there now lays”
.
🎥
©
Russian Military Historical Society

item.content:encoded:

🎙
Russian Ambassador to Seychelles Kirill Sokolov-Shcherbachev’s
comment
regarding Russia-Seychelles cooperation in the field of tourism
(4 September 2026)
#Tourism
💬
Tourism is the leading area of our cooperation with Seychelles
and it is now on the rise. For Seychelles tourism is the main source of income. The tourist industry suffered a lot when the air connectivity with Gulf countries was broken because of the Middle East crisis. Even after it has been partially restored,
that is Russia which kept providing Seychelles with the tourist flow
. Aeroflot flights have never stopped, although the flight time has increased.
#Aeroflot
Moreover, this year it has been decided to make
Aeroflot
flight
all year-round
, instead of seasonal timetable (September-May). After a short period,
flights have resumed on 8 July
. Currently, Aeroflot is operating
twice a week
and it is fully booked. In the winter period they add one more flight. 2025 counts
more than 43,000 passengers
, most of which are tourists. Guests from Russia make
15%
of the whole tourist flow
. Our country is on the third place after Germany and France. We will see what are the figures by the end of this year because, according to local estimates, sometimes
our tourists are ahead
.
#Russianlanguage
There are Russian-speaking tourist operators in Seychelles.
And the use of Russian language in the field of tourism is increasing.
We see Russian-speaking personnel in hotels and travel agencies, tour guides, advertisement etc. The Seychelles Tourism Academy (STA) is providing Russian language courses for more than
100 students
studying in different areas of tourist industry. It doesn’t mean that all of them will fluently speak Russian in a couple of months, but I am sure that
this is just the beginning
and it may be useful for some of them in their future professional activity.
Recently, we agreed the management of
Savoy
and
Coral Strand hotels
, which host a large number of Russians, and the STA to launch
a project for students
to help the reception desk in welcoming Russian guests and practicing their Russian language skills. Of course, we do not expect them to literally “sing” in Russian, they are just beginners. But anyway, I think this initiative is working for the nice image of the hotel and help the young specialists to overpass the language barrier. So, the Russian tourists, in particular those, who come to Seychelles in group by Aeroflot, can be warmly welcomed by Seychellois students at the hotel.
🤝
We count on keeping up the good figures in Russian arrivals and maybe even on their rise. At the same time we will continue to work on
further improving the tourist services
, for example, in expanding the Russian language in this field.
🇷🇺
🇸🇨
#RussiaSeychelles

item.description: ▪️ On September 8, 1941, the Siege of Leningrad began — one of the most horrific and tragic events not only of the Great Patriotic War but of the entire World War II. The siege lasted for 872 days and claimed the lives of approximately 1 million residents of the city, including more than 600'000 people who died from starvation. Alongside German troops, military units from European countries conquered by Hitler participated in the Siege of Leningrad — the 'Norway', 'the Netherlands' and 'Flanders' legions, as well as the Spanish infantry division. From the Narva direction, Baltic units — Latvian and Estonian battalions — were kept in reserve by the Nazis. From the north, the Finnish army besieged Leningrad and also shelled the city with its artillery. ▪️
On September 8, 1941, the
Siege of Leningrad began
— one of the most horrific and tragic events not only of the Great Patriotic War but of the entire World War II.
The siege lasted for 872 days and claimed the lives of approximately 1 million residents of the city, including more than
600'000 people
who died from starvation.
Alongside German troops, military units from European countries conquered by Hitler participated in the Siege of Leningrad —
the 'Norway', 'the Netherlands' and 'Flanders' legions,
as well as the Spanish infantry division. From the Narva direction, Baltic units —
Latvian and Estonian battalions
— were kept in reserve by the Nazis. From the north, the
Finnish army
besieged Leningrad and also shelled the city with its artillery.
The Nazis and their accomplices
planned to wipe Leningrad off the face of the Earth
and subject its population to
complete annihilation,
including by creating conditions for mass starvation, destroying food supplies, and cutting off supply routes.
***
In early September 1941, during the Leningrad Defensive Operation of the Red Army, the city was cut off by the Nazis from all land routes. On September 8, Hitler's troops captured Shlisselburg, completing the encirclement. The city was bombarded daily with artillery.
The Nazi command's orders were absolutely clear:
maintain the siege,
strictly enforce the blockade, shoot anyone crossing the front line, and bring about the total destruction of the city's population.
❗️
But Leningrad endured and never stopped fighting.
Under unbearable conditions, the city's industrial enterprises continued to operate. During the blockade, workers produced or repaired about
2'000 tanks, 1'500 aircraft, 850 warships and vessels
of various classes, as well as
225'000 submachine guns,
12'000 mortars, and 7.5 million shells and mines.
The most famous memorial to the victims of the blockade is the Piskaryovskoye Memorial Cemetery in Saint Petersburg — the largest mass military grave of World War II. Over
420'000 Leningrad residents and 70'000 defenders
of the city are buried there.
#Victory81
🌟
The blockade was finally lifted on
January 27, 1944,
during the Leningrad–Novgorod Offensive.
***
In 2022, at the request of the Prosecutor General’s Office of Russia, the Saint Petersburg City Court officially recognised the actions of the German occupying forces — along with their collaborators, including armed units formed in Belgium, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, Norway, and Finland, as well as individual volunteers from Austria, Latvia, Poland, France, and Czechoslovakia —
as a war crime, a crime against humanity, and an act of
genocide
against national and ethnic groups representing the population of the Soviet Union.
